decision.instructions: Does this shell command show the agent the text of a local project file (source, config, tests or docs), which is the read tool's job? A project file is one in the project's own tree, such as src/, crates/, packages/, docs/, or a named source or config file like package.json or Cargo.toml. A file downloaded or generated by the same command or session, a file under a run or scratch folder (such as $RUN or /tmp), and a log are not project files. YES: cat, head, tail, less, sed -n or awk given a project file path, or a Python or Node script that opens a project file and prints its text or a rewritten version of it. NO for everything else. In particular NO when head, tail, grep or sed only filter another command's output; for running a program or script; searches (rg, grep), listings and counts (ls, find, wc, stat); git commands; builds, tests, linters, formatters and compilers; package managers; remote content (gh api, curl, wget); queries that select fields from structured data (jq, json.load(...)['key']); and binary files.

positive.message: Chauffeur: Read project source, configuration, tests and docs with the read tool, not shell printers or Python/Node file reads, including scripts that print transformed source. Read the file first; use build tools for compilation and edit or patch tools for changes.

negative.message: Unused: this guard has no opinion on commands that do not bypass the read tool.

uncertain.message: Unused: an unsure answer leaves the command to the other contracts.

missing_evidence.message: Unused: an empty command is left to the other contracts.

judge_failure.message: Unused: a failed judgment is left to the other contracts.

cooldown.message: Unused: this contract has no cooldown.
